claims.claim_text: W-1 reported that the subject had pointed a handgun at her inside the residence at 615 South Resh Street, threatened to kill her and the neighbors, and fired a shot inside the home.
She stated that the subject owned two firearms and had not been taking his prescribed psychiatric medication.
At approximately 0005 hours on March 4, the Tactical Response Group was activated.
Upon arrival, SWAT officers immediately assumed control of the perimeter and positioned an armored vehicle in front of the residence.
I was designated as the primary negotiator and began PA announcements at approximately 0210 hours.
At approximately 0236 hours, the subject first appeared at the front door. He stepped onto the front porch, yelled at officers, and returned inside after approximately 45 seconds.
During the third appearance at 0251 hours, I observed the subject make a finger-gun gesture toward the armored vehicle, which I documented in my notes.

At approximately 0310 hours, in response to a recorded surrender request from W-1, the subject exited the front door holding what appeared to be an AR-15 style rifle. The subject held the weapon at his side and stood on the porch for approximately 15 seconds before returning inside without pointing the weapon at officers.
Immediately after this appearance, at approximately 0312 hours, the subject emerged again holding a small revolver in his left hand.
The subject raised the revolver, pointed it toward the sky, and then lowered it toward the armored vehicle.
An arrest team approached and found the subject seated against the front wall of the residence with the revolver on the ground beside him.
Officer Hassan deployed a 40 mm Less Lethal round as a precaution.
Anaheim Fire Department paramedics, who had been staged in the area, were summoned and arrived at approximately 0330 hours. The subject was pronounced deceased at approximately 0342 hours.
A search of the residence and porch area recovered one firearm: the .38 caliber Smith and Wesson revolver found beside the subject on the porch. No other firearms were located.
The K9 pulled the subject from the porch onto the front lawn.
